semantic_adjudication.reason: NL1 states the system enters Operate once powered on, and the contract's binding hints require an owner=system/root unconditional initial edge targeting Operate. The exact source inventory shows the only root-owned initial pseudostate edge is @initial:__root__ -> Off (tr_0001; also transition:line:24, [*] -> Off, triggered by keyOff, reachable_from_initial=false per verify_facts, which refutes it as a valid unconditional initial edge). This is a structural owner/target mismatch on the contract's own bound scope. The alternative two-step-paraphrase reading was considered as a potential undercutting alternative, but this obligation's supplied defeater_evidence_reference_catalog is empty, so no exact catalog token can be cited to support that alternative reading as surviving; absent such supplied evidence, the alternative cannot be sustained and is treated as defeated, leaving the exact structural mismatch established.

(3) NL-CONTRACT-REF-001 (root/system -> Operate initial entry) is NOT satisfied at the true root scope: the exact source inventory and closed model show the only unconditional root-owned initial edge is [*] -> Off (tr_0001 / transition:line:2 source; transition:line:24 keyOff-triggered in FCSTM), not an edge to Operate. This is a wrong-target/missing defect on the owner-local root initial edge relative to the contract's explicit target=Operate. (4) The Operate-owned initial edge nested contract (REF-010, alias for NL1-DERIVED-c43e6b268f28305677b3) targets Idle and is satisfied exactly by transition:line:15 ([*]->Idle inside Operate, verify_facts proved). (5) Containment contracts for Idle/Accelerating/Braking (REF-002/003/005) are satisfied by exact parent=Operate source rows and ModelIR nesting. (6) NL-CONTRACT-NL1-CONTAIN-CRUISE (REF-004) names 'Cruising' as a distinct child of Operate, but the exact source/model inventory has only one combined leaf state 'AcceleratingOrCruising' under Operate; there is no separate 'Cruising' state, so this containment obligation is missing a corresponding named element. (7) Cardinality contract REF-009 (Operate must have exactly Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking as direct children) is handled via cardinality_bindings below; the exact inventory shows only 3 direct children (Idle, AcceleratingOrCruising, Braking), not 4 distinctly named ones. (8) NL-CONTRACT-REF-008 (NL3 substate transition group) alternatives ALT-NL3-ACCEL/BRAKE/STOP are all realized by exact edges (tr_0005/0007/0008/0009 source; transition:line:16/17/18/19/20 closed), so no candidate needed for endpoint existence; but the 'Cruising' naming gap already covered by CONTAIN-CRUISE covers the naming mismatch. No additional_transition_groups needed. Additional_contracts: one derived initial_entry contract capturing the root-scope owner default-entry defect distinct from REF-001's literal target framing was not needed since REF-001 itself IS the exact root->Operate contract already supplied; I bind the candidate directly to REF-001 rather than deriving a duplicate.

issues.title: Root scope has no default/unconditional initial edge into Operate; root only unconditionally enters Off

issues.expected: On the keyOff signal while the system is in Operate (in any substate), the system transitions directly to the off/terminated condition.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM has no direct keyOff-triggered edge from Operate to Off. Instead, keyOff fires substate-local transitions Idle/AcceleratingOrCruising/Braking -> [*] (transition:line:12/13/14) with effect R45RouteToken=3, and only a separately guarded Operate -> Off transition (transition:line:23, guard R45RouteToken==3, solver_status=not_run) performs the actual move to Off. The keyOff-labeled edge into Off at root scope ([*] -> Off, transition:line:24) is an initial pseudostate edge flagged INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL and refuted by verify_facts, not a reachable runtime transition from Operate.
issues.reason: The NL obligation requires a keyOff-triggered transition from the Operate/powered-on condition to an off/terminated condition; the closed model implements this only through a multi-step effect+guard macro rather than a single direct edge, and the guard's satisfiability is not solver-verified, so the risk that completion never resolves must remain a candidate rather than be silently treated as satisfied.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The compiler-generated macro chain (local exit + effect + guarded completion transition) is the pyfcstm-standard lowering of a UML final-state exit from a composite with multiple substates; the working contract marks these as protected compiler-owned segments realizing one authored keyOff:Operate->Off transition (tr_0003), so the endpoint pair Operate->Off is arguably realized end-to-end when the guard deterministically holds after the effect fires.
issues.title: keyOff signal does not directly and unconditionally route Operate to the off/terminated condition

The alternative two-step-paraphrase reading was considered as a potential undercutting alternative, but this obligation's supplied defeater_evidence_reference_catalog is empty, so no exact catalog token can be cited to support that alternative reading as surviving; absent such supplied evidence, the alternative cannot be sustained and is treated as defeated, leaving the exact structural mismatch established.

NL3 gives a broad, underspecified statement about internal substate transitions driven by actions (accelerating, braking, stopping); it is represented as one general transition_endpoints obligation with hints reflecting the most textually supported exact pair (Idle to Accelerating) rather than manufacturing an exhaustive combinatorial set not explicitly stated, consistent with avoiding invented alternatives while still covering the segment. No cardinality, region, or explicit continuous state_action obligation is established by any segment: NL1 and NL3 only name states/substates and mention driving actions without requiring continuous performance of an activity, so no state_action contract was manufactured for Operate or its substates.
